intro: You're looking for a company commercial solicitor near you because your business needs legal help with a corporate transaction, a commercial contract, or both. Perhaps you're buying or selling a company, bringing in investors, or reviewing the terms you trade on. A local solicitor who understands company and commercial law can guide you through the documents and the process.
need_heading: What people searching for a company commercial solicitor usually need
need_lead: Company commercial solicitors handle the legal side of running and growing a business, from share sales to everyday contracts.
needs: You are buying or selling a business and need help with due diligence, the sale agreement, and the warranties and indemnities involved.
You are raising investment and need the share subscription documents, shareholder agreements, and articles of association prepared or reviewed carefully.
You need commercial contracts drafted or checked, such as terms of business, supply agreements, or distribution arrangements.
You are bringing in a new business partner or restructuring the company and need advice on the legal mechanics.
You want a solicitor who is local to you so you can meet in person and discuss sensitive business matters face to face.
context_heading: What to understand when searching for a company commercial solicitor near you
context: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland, solicitors are regulated by the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland by the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure; if that does not resolve things, the Legal Ombudsman can look at service complaints in England and Wales.

The word "lawyer" is not protected on its own, so check that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive (CILEx), or another authorised professional. Reserved activities such as conducting court litigation and certain probate and conveyancing work can only be carried out by authorised people.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of company you run and what the legal work relates to, such as a share sale, an investment round, or a commercial contract.
Mention whether you are buying or selling a business, and whether due diligence has already started.
Explain if the matter involves warranties and indemnities, and whether you need them reviewed or drafted.
Say whether you need help with a one-off transaction or ongoing commercial contract support.
Confirm your location and whether you need to meet the solicitor in person or are happy to work remotely.
Note any deadlines or key dates that the solicitor should know about, such as completion dates or investor timelines.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the company commercial solicitor
questions: Are you regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and can you provide your SRA number?
What experience do you have with the type of transaction I am involved in, such as share sales or investment rounds?
How will you handle due diligence, and what will you need from me?
Can you explain the warranties and indemnities in the draft agreement and what they mean for me?
Who will be my main point of contact, and how will you keep me updated?
What are your fees, and how will you bill me for the work?

faqs.q: Do I need a company commercial solicitor who is local to me?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but meeting in person can help with complex or sensitive business matters. A local solicitor may also be more familiar with the local business community, though this is not essential. Many solicitors now work effectively remotely.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a company commercial solicitor and a general practice solicitor?
faqs.a: Company commercial solicitors focus on business law, including corporate transactions and commercial contracts, while general practice solicitors may handle a wider range of personal and business matters. For specialised work like share sales or investment rounds, a company commercial solicitor is usually more appropriate.

faqs.q: How can I check that a solicitor is properly regulated?
faqs.a: In England and Wales, you can check the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) register. In Scotland, check with the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland with the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Always confirm that the person handling your matter is authorised.

faqs.q: What should I prepare before contacting a company commercial solicitor?
faqs.a: Gather any relevant documents, such as draft contracts, company accounts, or details of the transaction. Think about what you want to achieve and any deadlines. Being clear about your objectives will help the solicitor advise you efficiently.
